segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Giving newly rotated liaison officers the abbreviated instructions “usual Zone C protocol” and “standard muster point,” while assuming those local terms were self-explanatory despite having ample time.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Curse of Knowledge: the experienced briefer relies on facility-specific shorthand and assumes newly rotated liaisons share tacit operational knowledge; subsequent wrong-muster-point direction and terminology confusion support the mechanism.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Prioritizing the site facing the fastest-closing road access with two buses instead of splitting transport evenly across three sites.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: No hidden bias is assigned to decision point 3. The participant explicitly weighs closure risk and transport constraints to avoid stranding evacuees.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Suspending the exercise and transferring command to the Incident Commander with a written status briefing during degraded communications.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: No hidden bias is assigned to decision point 4. The written handoff is a deliberate reliability choice under degraded communications.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: An experienced briefer assumes newly rotated, less-informed liaison officers share tacit facility-specific knowledge and terminology, causing an under-explained briefing even when time is not a binding constraint.
